title.en: Kruskal, union-find and the cut property

summary: Show component membership as a first-class object so that rejecting an edge has a visible reason.
objective: Build a Kruskal walkthrough where each candidate edge is accepted or rejected because union-find says whether its endpoints already share a component.
intent_signals: Show why Kruskal rejects an edge.
Visualise connected components merging while building a spanning tree.
example_prompts: Build a Kruskal minimum spanning tree walkthrough with a component view and a sorted edge list.
Show the cut property on a selected component boundary.
negative_signals: Not a network design tool and not a routing recipe.
Not a claim about equal-weight graphs unless a tie rule is stated explicitly.
not_for: Not a network design tool and not a routing recipe.
Not a claim about equal-weight graphs unless a tie rule is stated explicitly.

entities.name: Weighted graph
entities.guidance: Place vertices in space with edges whose weights are readable labels, since the algorithm consumes edges in weight order.

entities.name: Component view
entities.guidance: Show each current component as a visually grouped set with its representative marked, so a union is a merge of two visible groups.

entities.name: Edge queue
entities.guidance: Display the sorted edge list with a cursor, so the next candidate is predictable and the ordering is auditable.

state_contract.model: A finite undirected, nonempty and connected edge-weighted graph with finite weights that may be zero or negative, a sorted edge list with a declared tie-breaking rule, a union-find structure over vertices, and an accepted edge set that stops at V minus one edges.
state_contract.authority: The union-find structure decides acceptance. Colours and grouping are rendered from it, so a visually merged group that union-find has not merged is a defect.
actions: Advance to the next candidate edge and see the find results.
Accept or step through automatically to completion.
Highlight a cut and inspect its minimum crossing edge.
Reset the graph, queue and components.

invariants: An edge is rejected exactly when its endpoints already have the same representative.
The accepted set never contains a cycle and finishes with V minus one edges on a connected graph.
Component grouping shown on screen always matches the current union-find state.
motion_guidance: Animate a union as two groups converging into one, so merging is an event rather than a recolour.
Keep rejected edges visible in a distinct state; erasing them hides why the tree looks the way it does.
known_limits: The cut property as cited assumes distinct edge weights; with ties the scene must state its tie-breaking rule.
Union-find path compression is an implementation detail that the display should not confuse with graph structure.
Disconnected input is either rejected or explicitly labelled a minimum spanning forest; the V minus one edge count applies to the connected case.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A minimum spanning tree is a spanning tree whose total weight is no larger than that of any other spanning tree, and given any cut in an edge-weighted graph with distinct weights the minimum-weight crossing edge belongs to the minimum spanning tree.
claims.scope: Distinct edge weights as cited; ties require a stated rule.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Minimum Spanning Trees, definition and cut property

claims.statement: Kruskal processes edges from smallest to largest weight, taking each edge that does not form a cycle with those already added and stopping after V minus one edges, using a union-find structure to identify cycle-forming edges, in time proportional to E log E in the worst case.
claims.scope: Connected edge-weighted graphs; the bound counts operations, not wall-clock time.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Minimum Spanning Trees, Kruskal algorithm and running time

object_craft.structure: Vertex spheres with label plates and edge tubes whose radius comes from a declared positive display mapping of the weight, so zero and negative weights stay drawable without altering the weight used by the algorithm.
object_craft.material: Neutral graph material with one accent for accepted edges and a distinct desaturated treatment for rejected ones.
object_craft.articulation: Edges do not move; only their state material changes.

object_craft.structure: A translucent hull or ring around each component with its representative vertex marked by a crown glyph.
object_craft.material: Component hulls use low opacity with distinct outlines so overlapping components remain separable.
object_craft.articulation: Hulls rebuild after each union and animate the merge.

physical_contract.scope: Discrete graph algorithm stepping; no physical layout forces unless declared separately.
checks: Rejections coincide exactly with equal representatives.
The run ends with V minus one accepted edges on a connected graph.
